title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study '½-simplicial' (semi-simplicial: face maps only, no degeneracies) complexes of k-modules L_• that are '∂-perfect', with a view to multiplicative structures. The previous page gives a structure theorem. A 'special' L_• is, up to isomorphism, a direct sum of standard pieces Λ^iΦ_• ⊗_k M_i (i ≥ 1) and Λ^jΨ_• ⊗_k N_j (j ≥ 0). Here Φ_n is free of rank n+1 (functions on the vertices of Δ^n) and Ψ_n is free of rank n, so that rank Λ^iΦ_n = C(n+1,i) and rank Λ^jΨ_n = C(n,j). The M_i and N_j are projective of finite type, and only finitely many are nonzero. 'Strictly special' adds that M_i and N_j are free.

Top lines. Strictly special is reformulated as L_• ≅ L°_• ⊗_Z k with L°_• a special ½-simplicial complex of Z-modules. So the strict notion is base change from Z.

Proposition 2. Special (resp. strictly special) ½-simplicial modules are stable under tensor product, i.e. the degreewise product (L⊗L')_n = L_n⊗L'_n. A bracketed, queried addition asks whether they are also stable under the tensor operations Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i. These are applied degreewise, as in Dold–Puppe's extension of non-additive functors.

The strict case reduces to the special case by working over Z.

Proof for tensor products. By additivity it suffices to treat the three products of generators:
- Λ^iΦ ⊗ Λ^jΦ (i, j ≥ 1),
- Λ^iΨ ⊗ Λ^jΨ (i, j ≥ 0),
- Λ^iΦ ⊗ Λ^jΨ (i ≥ 1, j ≥ 0).

These have free components of finite type. By 'Künneth–Eilenberg–Zilber' their invariants Π_i (the homology-type invariants used to characterise ∂-perfectness) are again free of finite type. It remains to show that only finitely many multiplicity modules M_i, N_j are nonzero.

The next page gives the argument as a growth count. The rank satisfies ρ(n) = Σ μ_i C(n+1,i) + Σ ν_j C(n,j), with μ_i = rk M_i and ν_j = rk N_j. Each nonzero μ_i or ν_j forces ρ(n) to grow at least like a polynomial of degree i or j. A tensor product of two generators has rank C(n+1,i)C(n+1,j) (or analogous), a polynomial of degree i+j. Since all contributions are nonnegative, only multiplicities of index ≤ i+j can be nonzero, so finitely many.

A crossed-out passage begins a lemma: given connectedness, the conditions of Cor. 2 of Prop. 1 are equivalent to (a) rk Π_i L_n being a polynomial in n, and (b) something 'for n large'. It is abandoned. The following page starts case 2°), Λ^k of a direct sum, reducing to Λ^k of Λ^•Φ ⊗ M and Λ^•Ψ ⊗ N.

The page serves a dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes in which a 'polynomial-growth / finitely many multiplicities' finiteness condition is shown to be closed under tensor and λ-type operations. This is presumably preparation for multiplicative (λ-ring / determinant-type) structures.
errors: The appeal to 'Künneth–Eilenberg–Zilber' is delicate in the semi-simplicial (no degeneracies) setting. The degreewise tensor product of semi-simplicial objects does not in general model the tensor product of associated chain complexes, since Eilenberg–Zilber uses degeneracies. Unless Π_i is an invariant for which this is verified directly on the standard pieces, this step is a gap.

The stability under Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i is only conjectured (bracketed with '?'). The left margin appears to carry a word like 'Inexact'/'faux' next to the statement, suggesting Grothendieck himself doubted or retracted part of Proposition 2, plausibly the Γ/Sym part.
The crossed-out lemma (equivalence with polynomiality of rk Π_i L_n) is abandoned unfinished; in its definition 'M_i = rg M_i' should read μ_i = rg M_i.

ideas.what: Structure/normal form of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules as finite sums Λ^iΦ⊗M_i ⊕ Λ^jΨ⊗N_j, with 'strictly special' meaning defined over Z
ideas.modern_name: classification of (projective) functors on Δ_inj^op / OI-type modules by standard 'exterior power' generators
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related to Dold–Kan-type theory and to Sam–Snowden-style OI-module theory (2010s)

ideas.what: Closure of the 'special' class under degreewise tensor product, proved by rank growth: rank of L_n is Σ μ_i C(n+1,i) + Σ ν_j C(n,j), and polynomial growth of bounded degree forces finitely many nonzero multiplicities
ideas.modern_name: polynomial growth / finite generation closure (cf. representation stability, FI/OI-modules)

ideas.what: Applying non-additive functors Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i degreewise to semi-simplicial complexes and asking whether the class is preserved
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe derived non-additive functors / λ-ring structure on a K-group of perfect complexes

ideas.what: Reduction of the strict (free) case to the case over Z by base change
ideas.modern_name: base change / descent of special objects from Z

missed.claim: Grothendieck characterises finiteness of a decomposition of semi-simplicial modules by polynomial growth of ranks in n, with binomial bases C(n+1,i), C(n,j). This is exactly the mechanism of later representation-stability theory (FI-/OI-modules), where Δ_inj^op-modules are close relatives. The link between ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and that theory does not seem to be made in the literature.
missed.quote: il reste à montrer qu'il n'y a que un nb fini de facteurs M_i, N_j ≠ 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would place this 1975–76 dévissage within the modern theory of polynomial functors on combinatorial categories, possibly giving a λ-ring/multiplicative structure on a Grothendieck group of such objects.

missed.claim: Stability of the special class under Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i is posed but queried (and possibly marked 'faux' in the margin). A lemma characterising Cor. 2 by polynomiality of rk Π_i L_n is begun and crossed out.
missed.quote: [et par les op. tensorielles Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i ?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Deciding which non-additive functors preserve the class is a concrete open-looking question about semi-simplicial λ-structures.

deep.surprise_reason: A technically interesting but local step in an unpublished dévissage. The polynomial-growth argument foreshadows representation-stability ideas, but it is a natural counting argument, not a striking new result.
transcription_corrections: The displayed modules should read Λ^iΦ_• ⊗ Λ^jΦ_• (i,j≥1), Λ^iΨ_• ⊗ Λ^jΨ_• (i,j≥0), Λ^iΦ_• ⊗ Λ^jΨ_• (i≥1, j≥0). The symbols are Φ and Ψ with index '•', not \mathcal{L}^*_α / α.
'(resp. th. spéciaux)' is likely '(resp. str. spéciaux)', i.e. strictement spéciaux.
In the crossed-out lemma, 'M_i = rg M_i et r_j = rg N_j' should be 'μ_i = rg M_i et ν_j = rg N_j'.
In the crossed-out lemma, 'rg Π_i L_α' should be 'rg Π_i L_n', and 'pour α grand' should be 'pour n grand'.
The left margin carries annotations (apparently 'Inexact?' and '[ ] faux') beside Proposition 2 that are omitted from the transcription.
